The record of acquisition provided reflected an inventory of 36 adult dogs. However, the inventory counted during the
inspection totaled 39 adult dogs. Additionally, the applicant had dispersed of three adult dogs since the previous
inspection and did not complete a disposition record for any of them. Inaccurate, missing, and/or incomplete records can
hinder various aspects of animal husbandry including the tracking and tracing of animals. To ensure accurate record
keeping the applicant shall maintain records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the required information for the
acquisition and disposition of animals.
To be corrected by 7.12.26

An enclosure of the outdoor portion of the sheltered facility, housing a litter of 12 week old Schnauzer puppies, had a
large hole in the gravel that allowed the puppies to move freely to an adjacent enclosure. It was observed during the
inspection that one of the young Schnauzers entered the enclosure through the hole. Animals not properly contained can
cause unwanted harm or allow other animals to enter the enclosure. The applicant must repair the hole or relocate the
animals to an enclosure that will contain the animals securely and restrict other animals from entering.
To be corrected by 7.10.26

The facility did not have medical records documenting the treatment of a 7-year-old female miniature schnauzer
(“Maggie”, m/c # 941000022078325). The most recent physical exam form, dated 6/16/26, includes a notation from the
Attending Veterinarian indicating that “Maggie” exhibited bilateral ear inflammation and prescribing treatment for her. The
treatment appears to have been completed as prescribed, as evidenced by the lack of visible ear inflammation as
observed by inspectors, but records of the treatments performed, and date of resolution were not documented in the dog’s
individual medical record or available for review at the time of the inspection.
Documentation of treatment for illness or injury must be kept and made available for APHIS officials to review and verify
that adequate veterinary care is provided to dogs who are ill or injured. These records must include the identity of the
animal, the date, a description of the problem, examination findings, test results, plan for treatment and care, and
treatment procedures performed.
To be corrected by: 7.12.26
This was a 2nd re-license inspection for a Class A license.
The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the applicant.
The applicant started the first inspection of the licensing process on 4/30/2026 and was given 60 days from that date
(6/30/26) to complete the process. The applicant has not demonstrated compliance with the Animal Welfare Act and has
not qualified for licensing at this time. The applicant must wait 6 months from 6/30/2026 to reapply. The license fee will not
be refunded or applied to the next application for licensure.
You may appeal this finding in writing by 7.9.2026. Appeals should be addressed to: USDA APHIS Animal Care, 2150
Centre Ave, Bldg B, Mailstop #3W11, Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117 or emailed to: animalcare@usda.gov
Conducting regulated activities without a valid USDA license is a violation of the Animal Welfare Act.
Additional Inspectors:
Lindsay Livingston, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
